grants: Nothing. The grid's terminal remains BLOCKED and its verdict remains T3_GRID_DECLARED_NO_CELL_EXECUTED.
why_this_exists: The programme ledger files P9.T3.FRONTIER.EXECUTION as an EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_BLOCKER requiring checkpoint, runtime and compute custody, and the acquisition audit initially read that as a download away from execution. Both are incomplete: the code that would run a cell does not exist.

what_the_freeze_already_provides.axes: 4 relational complexities x 7 representations x 6 scale points x 4 inference budgets x 2 domain blocks, at a fixed sample budget of 4
what_the_freeze_already_provides.analysis_side_complete: orion.study.p9.frontier_grid reads an outcome file and computes scale and compute frontiers, the on-grid rule, Holm-Bonferroni multiplicity and the crossing verdicts. It forbids extrapolation and interpolation and treats any declared cell absent from the outcome file as CANNOT_CHECK.

what_does_not_exist.evidence: Each name occurs only in the freeze document, in frontier_grid.py's declared axes, and in the status artifact. No serializer, no round-trip check, and no control construction exists anywhere in src/, papers/ or research/.

An EXECUTED cell must carry n_items and n_verified_correct. Nothing in the repository generates items at a given relational complexity k for the FORMAL_RELATIONAL and NON_FORMAL_PROCEDURAL blocks, and nothing verifies an answer to produce a verified count.

The freeze names orion.study.p9.frontier_grid as its runner, but that module's CLI takes --outcomes as an INPUT, documented as 'an outcome file for the declared cells; omit while none exists'. Nothing in the repository emits P9.UT3FrontierGridOutcomes.v1.

what_is_genuinely_available.checkpoints: All six declared ladder points resolve live. Qwen2.5 0.5B, 1.5B and 7B are Apache-2.0 and ungated; Qwen2.5-3B is ungated under a research licence; Llama-3.2 1B and 3B are gated=manual, free but requiring an accepted licence on an account.
what_is_genuinely_available.so: the acquisition half of the blocker is real but small; the construction half is the work.

build_order: 1. Item generator: produce items at each k for both domain blocks, each with a machine-checkable answer, so a verified count has a denominator that was fixed before any model saw it.

2. Representations: implement the seven, with the round-trip property the reversible one names, and with the two controls constructed so they cannot smuggle the signal the typed representations carry.
3. Runner: walk one cell, emit n_items and n_verified_correct, and mark every cell it did not run NOT_RUN, INFEASIBLE_RESOURCE or INFEASIBLE_CONTEXT with counts omitted.
4. Only then acquire checkpoints and execute.

prohibition.rule: No stub, mock or partial output may be written to the freeze's expected_result_artifact path.
prohibition.why: frontier_grid.py will compute a verdict from whatever outcome file it is handed, and the grid is a prospectively frozen gate. A stub reaching that path produces a fabricated result against a frozen claim. Development outputs go somewhere else and are labelled non-authoritative in-band.
prohibition.reinforced_by: the contract's own rule that a cell which did not run must omit its counts, because a number attached to a cell that did not run is the failure it exists to prevent

reclassification: Not externally blocked, and not one download from execution either. LOCALLY_UNEXECUTED with a substantial construction precondition.
